angle: Leaders must stage measurable productivity gains now, not bet on a distant step-change.
sourceTitle: Can AI Productivity Grow Fast Enough to Justify Big Tech’s Spending?
linkedinPost:
If your AI plan only pays off “once the foundation is done,” you don’t have a plan—you have a hope.

Knowledge at Wharton highlights a big question: can productivity gains grow fast enough to justify massive AI capex? That dilemma isn’t just for hyperscalers. It’s the same trap enterprises fall into with multi-year AI “platform first” programs that defer value until Phase 5.

My take: design for compounding ROI. Ship a measurable productivity lift every 90 days that also lays track for the next one.

How we do it on the ground:
- Define a hard operating metric (cycle time, handle time, rework rate) and target a 5–10% lift per quarter.
- Tie each lift to an asset that accrues (a reusable dataset, a decision service, a workflow pattern).
- Gate future funding on realized savings or revenue, not demos.

This approach makes the CFO an ally. Small wins stack. And if the curve never bends, you find out early and reallocate.

What is your next 90‑day, production‑measurable AI gain—and what asset will it leave behind? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #AITransformation
